report:
Reviewed the complete browser_delivery claim and all four tests plus the sole TODO implementation association. Baseline verification: the claim, implementation metadata and all test metadata match the historical packet; spec_plan.rs matches byte-for-byte. The book.rs delta changes review API/status fixtures and claim-fragment access in unrelated tests, not the three delivery tests or their helpers. Captured current fixture/process, chapter traversal and script-data decoding helpers through review read; these invoke the real preprocess binary and parse the emitted artifact rather than supplying canned results.

The ordinary self-contained-asset test asserts no external script/stylesheet references or unresolved template slots, exact recovery of script-sensitive model prose and Rust file contents, resolved Rust entity target, and chapter navigation mapping after a nested directory move. It supplies useful book packaging/data evidence, not proof that every interactive offline feature works. The invalid-model test asserts failure, specific diagnostics, empty stdout and absent explorer for unknown model types, missing Rust correspondence and cross-crate correspondence. The regeneration test asserts unchanged bytes and timestamp across identical preprocessing, then changed artifact and chapter content after a model edit. Thus these tests provide real partial evidence for offline packaging, validation before publishing, and rebuilt model snapshots.

Implementation remains explicitly TODO in spec_plan.rs; its paired browser_delivery_modes_share_a_validated_snapshot test deliberately has no assertions. Its documented prerequisite is the delivery integration stage that compares served/exported/book snapshots and exercises validation, offline browsing and regeneration. This reasonably reserves proof of the common resolved model/renderer across all three delivery modes, complete offline navigation/search/entity links/Rust source display, snapshot identification in each view, and both model and Rust edit visibility after rebuild/export/server restart. The existing book tests do not establish standalone/server parity, snapshot labels, Rust-edit regeneration, or interactive offline success; these remain deferred under that implementation/test pair, not approved as completed behavior. No N/A entries or unaccounted associated entries exist. No edits are required for accepting this explicitly deferred state.

Execution: personally ran review start/read and baseline comparison commands, and will record this report. No behavioral tests or workspace build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator reports 321 functional sage-meta tests and root cargo build passing; those are separate reported execution evidence, not the basis for relabeling TODO work.
